title: Autonomic VPC Route-Healer Terraform module: subnet routing, NAT/IGW orchestration, and endpoint health
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that manages VPC networking for Private deployments with built-in routing orchestration, NAT/IGW lifecycle hooks, VPC endpoint management, and automated route-health healing. The module should provide safe upgrade paths (zero-downtime where possible), integrated synthetic health probes for route and endpoint validation, strong observability hooks (logs/metrics) surfaced to Console, and CI gating to prevent unsafe plan changes.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for subnets (public/private/isolated), per-subnet route table assignment, and route priorities
Supports creating/configuring NAT Gateway pools and optional Internet Gateway with annotated lifecycle hooks for draining/replace operations
Creates VPC endpoints (Gateway and Interface) with configurable policies and route table associations; validates reachability via probes
Implements an automated route-healing controller (Terraform-null + Lambda or operator pattern) that can detect missing/blackholed routes and reconcile state
Upgrade plan includes a safe canary for route replacement and NAT swap with rollback hooks and state migration notes
Adds integration points for Console dashboards: route health metrics, synthetic probe failures, and per-change diff audit links
CI checks fail a plan that would delete all routes in a route table or remove all NAT gateways without a replacement
Documentation and example usage for Dedicated and Private VPC topologies in repo/examples and internal module registry
steps: Draft module interface (variables/outputs) and share with infra-platform and security for review
Implement core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet (multi-az), aws_route_table, aws_route, aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway, aws_vpc_endpoint
Add optional egress proxy pattern: support for NAT Gateway autoscaling pattern vs Transit Gateway egress in later phases
Implement health probes: synthetic private EC2 task + Lambda that tests endpoint and route reachability, push metrics to CloudWatch and Console
Implement Terraform lifecycle & provisioner hooks that trigger graceful drain scripts for NAT swap operations
Add a small operator (null_resource + remote-exec OR Lambda) for auto-repairing accidental route deletions discovered by probes
Add terraform plan/validate checks in CI (pre-commit + pipeline) to block dangerous diffs
Write docs, example stacks, and migration guide for existing Private customers
Run canary in staging (two clusters) then roll to Dedicated schedules after 2 weeks of zero probe failures
notes: This module intentionally separates control-plane resources (route tables, endpoints) from ephemeral egress resources (NAT gateways) to make safe upgrades easier. We will provide a migration helper script for customers that still use single-NAT patterns. Consider IPv6 egress options (egress-only IGW) in follow-up.
rollout_plan: Stage1 - internal infra team deploy to staging-private-1 (single AZ) with feature flag enabled
Stage2 - run synthetic probes for 7 days, monitor Console metrics for probe_latency and probe_failures
Stage3 - canary to two Dedicated customers (coord with Customer Success) with scheduled maintenance windows
Stage4 - global rollout with automated migration helper and runbook
test_plan: Unit: terraform fmt + validate + module-level terratest for resource creation
Integration: deploy example stacks to staging and run probe suite (routing, endpoint policy enforcement, S3 access via gateway endpoint)
Chaos: simulate route deletion and NAT termination to verify auto-repair and graceful failover
Policy: run policy checks that ensure no unrestricted 0.0.0.0/0 routes are accidentally added to isolated subnets
